Am I right in thinking that this will cause issues if the development device supports fp16 while the target device does not? This seems like it will only bake the variant that is supported by the development device.

I ran into a similar problem for baking too, so I introduced the idea of a "profile", so you can generate the baked source for a specific platform and Apple GPU:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5a30a7e7cd5d5f0f8cb019d4765a46219ecf8e56/drivers/metal/rendering_shader_container_metal.h#L85

The idea being that when baking, the exporter can specify a platform:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5a30a7e7cd5d5f0f8cb019d4765a46219ecf8e56/drivers/metal/rendering_shader_container_metal.h#L51-L54

and minimum GPU:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5a30a7e7cd5d5f0f8cb019d4765a46219ecf8e56/drivers/metal/rendering_shader_container_metal.h#L56-L67

and that will determine the capabilities and features that the SPIR-V → Metal translation can use. This is added to the container:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5a30a7e7cd5d5f0f8cb019d4765a46219ecf8e56/drivers/metal/rendering_shader_container_metal.h#L226
My future thought is that we could bake multiple versions, so that depending on the device, it will load the correct baked version of the shaders.
All variants available in the shader are baked unless explicitly disabled, so this won't cause issues. We don't need the FP16 support available on the host device to be able to compile the SPIR-V.

To be a bit clearer, this is a good example of the conversion process that happened. If something was being detected in the host as a capability, it was turned into a variant instead. The baker scans all enabled variants and compiles them. Both FP16 and non-FP16 variants are shipped in the container.

The client machine picks the right variant based on the presence of FP16 support on the hardware.

> My future thought is that we could bake multiple versions, so that depending on the device, it will load the correct baked version of the shaders.

This is pretty much exactly what happens already and is demonstrated in the FSR2 code. If you ran into a specific problem that it doesn't let you do that, it's because there's something on the pipeline that is dependent on the host to generate it. That is not the case for glslang, you can very much compile SPIR-V with hardware capabilities not available in the system.
